API-get-user.rationale: `Notion | Retrieve a user` reads a user object from the user's Notion integration context, so it can return non-public workspace/account data. User profile fields such as names may be authored by workspace users; because the advertised text does not give an output schema or say profiles are trusted, UNTRUSTED is kept on the least-restrictive reading.

API-get-users.rationale: `Notion | List all users` reads the workspace user list through Notion credentials, so it can return non-public SaaS data. Listed users' profile names/metadata may be authored by other workspace users; output details are not advertised, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

API-get-self.rationale: `Notion | Retrieve your token's bot user` returns metadata about the authenticated token's bot user, which is non-public SaaS/account data. The text does not show an output schema, so identifier fields are inferred.

API-post-search.rationale: `Notion | Search by title` returns pages or data sources visible to the integration, which may be non-public. Titles and database/page metadata can be authored in multi-writer Notion content, so results are UNTRUSTED. Although it is a POST, the advertised operation is search/read rather than state change.

API-get-block-children.rationale: `Notion | Retrieve block children` reads block/page content visible to the integration, which can be non-public. Child block text and metadata in a multi-writer Notion page may be attacker-authored, so it is UNTRUSTED.

API-patch-block-children.rationale: `Notion | Append block children` writes `Child content to append` to a Notion `block_id`/page. If that block/page is shared or public, the write can deliver agent-supplied content to an attacker-readable place; the advertisement does not rule this out, so SINK is kept. The response may include Notion object data and content from multi-writer pages, so SECRET/UNTRUSTED are kept on the least-restrictive reading.

API-retrieve-a-block.rationale: `Notion | Retrieve a block` reads a Notion block visible to the integration. Block text/media metadata can be non-public and can be authored by other collaborators, so SECRET and UNTRUSTED apply.

API-update-a-block.rationale: `Notion | Update a block` can change a `Notion block`, including `text` or `checked`, and can `archive (delete)` it. Writes to a shared/public Notion block could be attacker-readable, which the text does not exclude. Returned block data may be non-public and may contain collaborator-authored content.

API-delete-a-block.rationale: `Notion | Delete a block` changes Notion state for the selected `Notion block`. If the block is in an attacker-readable shared/public page, the state change is observable; the advertised text does not rule this out. Any returned block object may include non-public or collaborator-authored metadata/content.

API-retrieve-a-page.rationale: `Notion | Retrieve a page` reads a page by `Identifier for a Notion page`, including page properties. Page titles/properties can be private and can be authored by collaborators in multi-writer Notion content.

API-patch-page.rationale: `Notion | Update page properties` changes the selected page's `property values`, trash/archive status, `icon`, or `cover`. If the page is shared/public, these values can be attacker-readable; the text does not exclude that. The operation can also return non-public page data containing collaborator-authored properties.

API-post-page.rationale: `Notion | Create a page` writes a new page under `parent` with `properties`, `children`, `icon`, and `cover`. A parent may be a shared/public page or data source, so the new content can be attacker-readable; the text does not restrict this. Returned page data can be non-public and may include untrusted Notion content/metadata.

API-retrieve-a-page-property.rationale: `Notion | Retrieve a page property item` reads a property from a Notion page. Property values may be non-public and may be authored in a multi-writer page or database, so SECRET and UNTRUSTED apply.

API-retrieve-a-comment.rationale: `Notion | Retrieve comments` reads comments for a `Notion block or page`. Comments are explicitly multi-writer content and may contain attacker-authored text and author identifiers, while also being non-public workspace data.

API-create-a-comment.rationale: `Notion | Create comment` writes `The content of the comment` to the specified page `parent`. If that page is shared/public or otherwise attacker-readable, this can deliver agent-supplied data to an attacker; the text does not rule that out. Returned comment data can include non-public Notion metadata and comment/author fields.

API-query-data-source.rationale: `Notion | Query a data source` reads pages/rows from a Notion `data source (database)`. Database contents and properties may be non-public and collaborator-authored, so results are SECRET and UNTRUSTED. Despite the destructive hint, the advertised action is `Query`, so kind is READ.

API-retrieve-a-data-source.rationale: `Notion | Retrieve a data source` reads Notion data-source schema/metadata. Titles, descriptions, and property names can be non-public and can be authored by collaborators, so SECRET and UNTRUSTED apply.

API-update-a-data-source.rationale: `Notion | Update a data source` writes `title`, `description`, and `Property schema updates` for the selected data source. If the data source is shared/public, these writes can be attacker-readable; the text does not exclude this. Returned data-source metadata may be non-public and may include collaborator-authored fields.

API-create-a-data-source.rationale: `Notion | Create a data source` writes a new data source under `parent` with `Property schema` and `title`. If the parent is shared/public, the new schema/title can be attacker-readable; the text does not restrict the parent to private locations. Returned metadata may be non-public/untrusted.

API-list-data-source-templates.rationale: `Notion | List templates in a data source` reads templates from a Notion data source. Template names/content/metadata may be non-public and authored by collaborators, so SECRET and UNTRUSTED apply.

API-retrieve-a-database.rationale: `Notion | Retrieve a database` reads a Notion database by identifier. Database titles, descriptions, and property names can be non-public and collaborator-authored, so SECRET and UNTRUSTED apply.

API-move-page.rationale: `Notion | Move a page` changes the selected page's `parent`. Moving a page into a shared/public parent could make the page or the state change attacker-readable; the text does not rule this out. Returned page metadata may be non-public and may include collaborator-authored fields.

API-retrieve-page-markdown.rationale: `Notion | Retrieve a page as Markdown` reads the page content, and the errors mention pages `not shared with the integration`, confirming integration-scoped non-public access. Markdown page content, and optional `meeting note transcripts`, can contain collaborator-authored text, so it is UNTRUSTED.

API-update-page-markdown.rationale: `Notion | Update a page's content as Markdown` can `replace`, `update`, `insert`, or `replace` ranges of page content for a `Notion page (or block)`. If the page is shared/public, the Markdown supplied by the agent can be attacker-readable; the text does not exclude that. The operation also has integration-scoped access to page content, and returned content/metadata may include collaborator-authored text.

notes: No output schemas are advertised. Output-field lists are therefore inferred from the advertised Notion object types and argument names, and all affected tools are marked undetermined where exact returned fields or public/shared visibility are not settled by the description.
